rules.text: Systems worksurfaces with 1/2" Cord Drop allow cords to drop below the worksurface at any point along the back edge; Full Depth worksurfaces fit flush against panels and cords/cables are routed through cable scallops.

Laminate worksurfaces: front (user's) edge available in 3 mm edge profile or P-edge profile; knife edge with 3 mm user edge is available on straight and tapered systems worksurfaces and on round tables. Back and side edges are flat.
Wood veneer worksurfaces have a square (3 mm) edge profile only on the front edge; back edge and edges that join adjacent worksurfaces are flat; wood edge color matches worksurface finish.
Edge profile finishes are specified separately from laminate color. Edge profile is applied to front (user's) edge only.
Cable scallops allow cords and plugs to pass behind the worksurface; cable scallops can be omitted as an option.
PVC-free 3 mm edge profiles are proprietary polyolefin blend for all solid colors and seven woodgrain finishes; matching 1 mm side and back edges are also PVC-free.
P-edge profile worksurface depths are 3/8" deeper than 3 mm edge profile worksurfaces; both provide a flush interface with universal pedestals.

Keyboard surface on dual worksurface adjusts up to 6" higher or 5" lower than the monitor worksurface; tilts with a range of 25° (+15°/-10°). A 1" gap separates keyboard surface sides from adjacent worksurfaces; 1 1/2" space between keyboard and monitor surfaces.

30"D straight, tapered, and transition cantilevered worksurfaces require additional floor support along the front edge, such as a pedestal, end panel, post leg, side support bracket, or an adjacent return worksurface.
Taper-flat worksurfaces can be supported at the larger end with a side support bracket and a post leg. If the larger end is 30"D, a 24"D end panel can also be used.

Spanner worksurfaces with 3" notch accommodate Answer panels; legs and cantilevers or column and cantilevers must be used for support. Notch is not included on spanner worksurfaces for freestanding applications without panels.

3 mm edge bullet peninsula, jetty, and bubble jetty worksurfaces can be supported two ways: (a) a cantilever, a center support panel and a column; or (b) a cantilever, a side support bracket, and two post legs.

A center support panel should not be used (unfinished top edge would be exposed) for: bullet peninsula with P-edge, jetty with P-edge, bubble jetty with P-edge, angled peninsula with 3 mm edge and 1/2" cord drop. Use a cantilever, a side support bracket, and two post legs instead.

Linking peninsula and linking worksurfaces with 3" notch accommodate Answer panels. Legs and cantilevers or column and cantilevers must be used to support linking peninsula worksurfaces. One leg and two cantilevers must be used to support linking worksurfaces.
3 mm edge visitor worksurfaces must be supported by either a cantilever and a center support panel, or by a cantilever, a side support bracket, and a leg.

In P-edge profile worksurface applications (visitor), a side support bracket, a cantilever, and a leg must be used for support; a center support panel should not be used because its unfinished top edge would be exposed.
Worksurfaces can be used freestanding or in panel-supported installations. Supports are ordered separately and installed in the field.

Panel-supported applications can use: closed loop, open loop, half loop, intermediate support, off-module worksurface-to-panel connector, side support brackets, cantilever with tie plate, end panel, standing-height end panel, support plate, center support panel with tie plate, standing-height center support panel with tie plate, columns or legs, Universal pedestal with filler, Universal lateral file with underworksurface lateral file filler.

Tip: Selected worksurfaces with P-edge profile include alignment slots to accept cabby legs for column support: use two legs for panel-mounted spanner, bullet peninsula, linking peninsula, jetty, and bubble jetty worksurfaces; use one leg for visitor and linking worksurfaces.

Answer Freestanding desk applications can use: end supports, peninsula supports, corner support, columns and legs, closed loop or open loop, modesty panels, pedestals, lateral files and storage cabinets (see Answer Freestanding Specification Guide).
Answer Freestanding peninsula support is not compatible with P-edge bullet peninsula, jetty, or bubble jetty worksurfaces. Legs or other alternate supports are recommended.

Leg-based applications can use: closed loop, open loop, intermediate support, post legs, double post leg, double post C-leg, support plate. Pedestal can also be used in leg-based freestanding installations.
Intermediate supports replace the need for other types of worksurface support when used with 1-High or 1.5-High Universal storage.

Long worksurface spans must be supported with cantilevers, pedestals, legs, or other supports at least every 54". Reinforcing channel (TS7WKSPT) allows the distance between supports to be increased to 60" for heavily loaded worksurfaces, or up to 72" for lighter expected loads. Reinforcing channel must be specified separately.
Knife edge worksurfaces require reinforcement channels for unsupported spans greater than 48": TS7WKSPT39 for 54"W, TS7WKSPT for 60"W and 66"W, TS7WKSPT72 for 72"W worksurfaces.
Soft edge worksurfaces and power and data access door and tray worksurfaces require reinforcement channel or other support on worksurfaces 60" or larger.
Worksurface depth is 1/2" less than nominal (cord drop) and allows cords and cables to pass over at any point. Cable scallops provide space for plugs to pass over the back edge.

Worksurface wire managers convert cable scallops into grommets in freestanding applications. Wire managers are included with wood veneer worksurfaces; wire managers for laminate worksurfaces must be ordered separately (TS7WWM).

Corner worksurfaces have scallops located 12 1/2" from the rear corner to the center of the scallop. Taper-flat worksurfaces have a single scallop located 18 1/2" from the larger end. Scallops are centered on the rear edge of all other worksurfaces that include them.
Cable scallop can be omitted for freestanding applications or panel-supported applications where plugs do not need to pass over the back edge.

Laminate worksurfaces: laminate; Open Line laminate (option, non-Steelcase laminates). Front edge: plastic; back and side edges: plastic color defaults to match user's edge. Wood veneer worksurfaces: wood veneer (standard), Customiz stain (option), full-fill finish (option); square (3 mm) edge profile wood veneer to match worksurface; front edge wood edge band.

P-edge profiles produce a valley when installed perpendicular to adjacent worksurfaces. The additional 3/8" depth of P-edge profiles causes an interference fit in on-module panel-mounted applications. For L-configurations using two worksurfaces, the 3 mm edge profile is recommended.

P-edge profile worksurface depth prevents modesty panels from fitting properly in return or bridge Answer Freestanding desk applications. Modesty panels cannot be used when a return or bridge worksurface is attached to the front edge of a P-edge worksurface. 3 mm edge profile recommended for return or bridge applications.
Full-depth worksurfaces provide an uninterrupted working surface and allow traditional corner or L-configuration planning without uneven gaps.

Plan using worksurface actual dimensions when panel-wrapping. Straight and transition worksurfaces are full-width to correspond directly with panel width. Corner, extended corner, 120° corner, bullet peninsula, jetty, visitor, and linking worksurfaces are 1/2" less than panel width to allow a consistent 1/2" cable-management gap when used with straight worksurfaces.
Tip: To avoid uneven gaps in panel-supported applications, use full-depth worksurfaces to create L-configurations.
Screens mount to worksurfaces in privacy position or below the worksurface for modesty (see Screens, page 586).
Worksurfaces used in panel-supported installations must follow applicable panel stability guidelines (page 124).

Do not use a Universal Systems Worksurface as a top for storage that matches the worksurface width; worksurfaces are slightly undersized for panel-wrapped applications and will not fit over full-width storage. Use field-installed storage tops.
Knife edge worksurfaces have limitations for support options and application restrictions (see page 226).

Identical worksurfaces ordered on the same line item are packed on pallets containing 5–50 worksurfaces depending on size; remaining are packed individually in cartons. If palletizing is not desired, order in quantities of four or less per line item. Wood veneer worksurfaces cannot be palletized.

Soft edge and power and data access door and tray are available on straight and taper Universal Systems Worksurfaces with 1/2" cord drop and full depth. Personal caddy is available on straight Universal Systems Worksurfaces with 1/2" cord drop and full depth.

Door/tray cutout is optional; power and data access door and tray is ordered separately. 24"W cutout is centered near the back of the worksurface. Caddy cutout is optional; personal caddy is ordered separately; cutout is available on the left- or right-hand side.
Soft edge is 36" wide centered on the worksurface; balance of front edge is 3 mm radius. Back and side edges are flat.

Availability matrix (1 = only soft edge, only power & data access door & tray, or both; 2 = only personal caddy; 3 = personal caddy and power & data access door & tray; 4 = soft edge, door & tray, and personal caddy): Straights 23 1/2"D/24"D and 29 1/2"D/30"D — 48"W: 1; 54"W: 1,2; 60"W: 1,2; 66"W: 1,2,3; 72"W: 1,2,3,4; 78"W, 84"W, 90"W, 96"W: 1. Tapered 29 1/2"D or 30"D to 23 1/2"D or 24"D — 48"W: 1; 60"W: 1; 72"W: 1.
Power and data access door and tray is available with cord or with modular or hardwire connection. Tray includes six simplex receptacles and cutout for data access.
Soft edge profile is polyurethane and is available with Bactiblock antimicrobial protection. Scallops are omitted on worksurface when door and tray cutout option is selected.

Data cutout in tray can accommodate either a single gang or a modular furniture communication faceplate; tray includes adapter for modular faceplate. Filler packages (FMVF) fill unused data cutouts; order separately in packages of 20.
Corded version includes 10' cord with plug. Modular and hardwire versions each include 8' of harness. Non-PVC versions are available for each power solution.

Three wiring schematics are available in the modular version – 3+1, 2+2, and 3 separate neutrals (3SN). Each has a single circuit. 3+1 and 2+2 have the option for line 1, 2, 3, or 4 with either a system or isolated ground. 3SN has the option for line 1, 2, or 3 with either a system or isolated ground.

With the modular and hardwire version, the harness enters the panel through a field cut opening in a fabric skin; a grommet is included to provide a finished edge. Inside the panel the harness can connect to a powerkit or it can use either a harness to harness connector or a branching harness to harness connector to connect to other modular harness trays or modular harnesses.
Cord and plug version has an integrated overload circuit breaker.
Caddy is available in three molded plastic colors: Midnight, Platinum Solid, and Arctic White; pad is Grey V5.
Fixed storage can be used with worksurfaces with soft edge but must not encroach the 36" width of the edge. Worksurfaces connected perpendicular should not encroach the 36" width of the soft edge.

Soft edge worksurfaces are available with the same support options and follow the same application rules as other Universal Systems worksurfaces. Exception: 48"W worksurface with soft edge used with the FrameOne post leg has some limitations.

In an end-of-run condition, the FrameOne post leg will not fit when used with 48"W soft edge worksurfaces; use half, open, or closed loop legs. In shared applications, the FrameOne post leg can be angled and positioned at the front edge or for a square orientation it must be inset 1" from the front edge when used with 48"W soft edge worksurfaces.

Access holes in tray allow power and data to be routed straight back when worksurface is against the panel or routed to the sides when the worksurface is perpendicular to the panel. Worksurfaces with power and data access door and tray follow the same support options and application rules as other Universal Systems worksurfaces.

Tray with cord and plug can be used in a freestanding table application. Worksurfaces with power and data access door and tray with modular or hardwire power cannot be used in a freestanding application: the worksurface must either be attached to a panel on one end, or if attached to low storage with an intermediate support on one end, the cabinet must be attached to the panel or ganged to another storage cabinet. Applies to both parallel and perpendicular to the panel applications.

Height of tray is 4 3/4" so lower storage height must be accounted for when used adjacent to tray. Width of outer tray below the worksurface is 27 1/8" so adjacent lower storage dimensions must be accounted for on each worksurface width.
Tray with modular or hardwire harness includes two harness clips; tray with cord and plug includes two cord clips.
Soft edge worksurfaces and power and data access door and tray worksurfaces require reinforcement channel or other support on worksurfaces 60"W or larger.

Personal caddy is available on straight worksurfaces with 3 mm, soft or wood square edges, 24"D or 30"D. Caddy is available on worksurfaces 54"W to 72"W (if only with caddy), 66"W and 72"W (if with tray and caddy), and 72"W (if with soft edge and caddy).

Worksurface and caddy bracing is included with the caddy package. Two brace lengths are available and length is specified as an option: the shorter brace fits 54"W and 60"W worksurfaces; the longer brace fits 66"W and 72"W.

Tip: In panel-mounted applications where a 24"D worksurface is applied parallel to the panel, the caddy brace will interfere with panel-mounted cantilevers that are within 54" of the side edge of the worksurface where the caddy is positioned. Use center support panel as an alternative in this condition.
Worksurfaces greater than 72"W (with caddy) require additional support such as cantilevers, pedestals, or legs beyond the brace.
Caddy cutout is 6 5/8" from edge of worksurface, bracing is 5 1/2" from the edge.

FrameOne legs for Universal (closed, open, and half loops) work in conjunction with personal caddy. FrameOne post version only works in shared worksurface applications where the leg is angled to the front edge of the worksurface. Cabby leg will work on worksurfaces with personal caddy only if leg is in 90° orientation. Universal double post leg will work in shared worksurface applications. Tip: Legs other than those shown will not work adjacent to the personal caddy.
Front edge support is recommended if two caddies are planned side-by-side.

Chicago, New York, and Los Angeles have special requirements. The power and data tray is UL listed, designed to meet U.S. and Canadian national electrical and energy codes and most local building codes; consult local authority having jurisdiction.

Soft edge: 6615 Grey V5 plastic. Door: paint or anodized aluminum. Door bezel: 6694 Slate plastic. Inner and outer tray: 7237 Slate paint. End caps for outer tray: 6694 Slate plastic. Panel grommet plastic: 6000 Black, 6009 Arctic White, 6249 Platinum Solid, 6654 Sand, 6697 Fog. Personal caddy plastic: 6009 Arctic White, 6249 Platinum Solid, 6695 Midnight; pad 6615 Grey V5.

Transaction worksurface provides a surface for standing visitors or a shelf. Attachment brackets are included. Shortened top caps are included; available in thin, square, or oval styles, compatible with same-height or change-of-height applications.
Edge profile (3 mm or P-edge, plastic, or wood 3 mm) is applied to all edges; plastic edges specified separately from laminate color.
Tip: Wood veneer transaction worksurfaces are not available in 23"W.
Transaction worksurface support brackets connect to the top of a horizontal connecting bar. Horizontal bar must be connected to junctions in top position.
Transaction worksurfaces cannot be used when a transparent window, pass-thru window, or consolidation point cabinet are assembled at the top of a panel.
In square and oval trim applications, a transaction top cannot be used on a 48"H panel when the panel is connected to a taller panel in a change-of-height condition.

Spanning two panels is possible with thin trim (28" over 30"; 34" over 18"+18"; 40" over 18"+24"; 46" over 24"+24"). Exception: 58"W transaction worksurface cannot span multi-panels (additional support bracket conflicts with junction between two 30"W panels).

Spanning two panels is possible with square or oval trim (23" over 30"; 29" over 18"+18"; 35" over 18"+24"; 41" over 24"+24"). Exception: 53"W transaction worksurface cannot span multi-panels (additional support bracket conflicts with the junction between two 30"W panels).
Width of transaction worksurface with thin trim is 2" shorter than the width of corresponding panel; with square and oval trim it is 7" shorter, to accommodate change-of-height applications.

Panels on one or both sides of the transaction worksurface can be higher or lower than the panel that supports it. Thin or oval trim transaction worksurfaces include top trim that accommodates all standard and change-of-height applications (one end or both ends). Square trim transaction worksurfaces include top trim for standard and slim change-of-height applications; change-of-height option must be specified when used adjacent to cable management change-of-height (one end or both ends).
Recommended standing height for transaction worksurface is achieved by attaching it to 42"H panels.
Transaction worksurface must be centered on the panel.

Utility2 shelf lights can be installed beneath transaction worksurfaces using screws and keyhole slots in light fixture. Transaction worksurface blocks cable routing in the top cable tray but cable routing is still available lower in the panel.

Surface materials: laminate or Open Line laminate; edges plastic; top caps paint or wood; support brackets black paint only; wood veneer (standard), Customiz stain, full-fill finish; square (3 mm) edge wood veneer to match.
On-module supports can be used to panel support worksurfaces in various configurations; they engage the slots in the vertical uprights of Answer panels.
Worksurface supports feature an alignment tab used to set a depth for Universal Systems Worksurfaces with 1/2" cord drop. This tab is bent down when installing full-depth worksurfaces.
Cantilever can panel-support a worksurface at any height. End panel can support the end of a worksurface. Center support panel can be shared by two worksurfaces and may be required for longer runs.

Side support brackets support the ends of straight and corner worksurfaces and the back corner of any corner worksurface; support worksurfaces at any height in 1" increments; ship as a left- and right-hand pair and are ordered separately. They can support the end of a worksurface wrapped by a panel with the same width dimension that matches the worksurface depth.

Single side support bracket can support the rear corner of corner, extended corner, and 120° corner worksurfaces, and the user's side rear corner of bullet peninsula, angled peninsula, visitor, jetty, and bubble jetty worksurfaces. Tip: For off-module fin wall applications, the single side support bracket must be handed appropriately for connection to the fin wall.

Cantilevers support worksurfaces at any height in 1" increments; cantilever is non-handed and can support either end of a worksurface, or be shared to support two worksurfaces at the same height simultaneously. One tie plate ships with each cantilever.

Adjacent cantilevered worksurfaces must be the same height in order to connect with a tie plate and provide panel stability. Tip: Answer panel junctions can accommodate only one support at each worksurface seam.

Center support panel is an alternative to a cantilever in supporting longer runs of worksurfaces for additional panel stability. Center support panels are available in seated and standing heights, cannot be used in freestanding applications or as a substitute for an end panel. One tie plate ships with each center support panel.

Center support panels should not be installed along the user's edge on P-edge profile jetty and visitor worksurfaces (unfinished top edge exposed). Use single side support bracket and a post or cabby leg.
End panels can support the end of a worksurface for additional panel stability; available in seated and standing heights, and cannot be used in freestanding applications.

Pedestals and lateral files with a filler can support the end of a worksurface in place of an end panel. All panel mounted supports can be removed and repositioned later without permanent damage to panels or skins.
Side support bracket and reinforcing channel: black paint only. Cantilever, center support panel, and end panel: paint.

Off-module worksurface-to-panel connector connects 18"D, 24"D, and 30"D worksurfaces to wider panels, eliminating the need to match panel width to worksurface depth. Replaces side supports, cantilevers, and the need for front edge support with 30"D worksurfaces. Connector attaches into the slotted channels of the panel junctions.
Worksurface can be positioned anywhere along the width of the off-module connector.
Off-module worksurface to panel connector cannot be used at the same elevation on adjacent inline panels.
Off-module worksurface to panel connector can support a single worksurface only.
Off-module worksurface to panel connector cannot replace cantilevers and side support brackets when worksurface is parallel to the panel.

Off-module worksurface to panel connector cannot be used in front of or on the adjacent panel next to a 12"H or a 24"H slatwall skin positioned in the second 12" skin module from the base of the panel.

FrameOne legs and supports share a common visual with FrameOne bench and support Universal worksurfaces in freestanding, storage-supported, or panel-supported applications. Spacers between top of legs and worksurface provide a floating look.

Closed, open, and half-loop legs are handed when panel supporting and must be specified left or right when facing the front of the worksurface. Freestanding tethered and table versions are non-handed.
Closed, open, and half-loop legs in panel supporting versions support the ends of worksurface; they are not shared supports between two worksurfaces.
Closed and open-loop legs are available in tethered versions in which one side of the worksurface is attached to a panel or storage.
Intermediate support is used with Universal One-High or 1.5-High storage as a worksurface support allowing for nesting of low storage. Post leg is square and can be used as a column support.
Closed and open-loop legs are available in table versions in which both sides of the worksurface are supported by the legs. Post legs can also be used to create freestanding tables.
Half-loop leg is always panel supporting; however panels cannot exceed 48"H or support overhead storage above.
Closed, open, and half-loop legs do not align properly with knife-edge worksurfaces; use cantilevers instead (see page 226).

27"H mobile, freestanding, or fixed pedestals do not fit flush to the inside of the closed, open, or half-loop leg (3" gap due to worksurface support plate); 25 1/2"H freestanding pedestals or 21"H mobile pedestals will fit flush.

27"H mobile, freestanding, or fixed pedestals do not fit flush to the inside of the post leg (5 3/4" gap due to worksurface support plate); 25 1/2"H freestanding pedestals or 21"H mobile pedestals will fit flush.
Post leg can be shared between two worksurfaces; in shared applications it can be square or oriented angled to the front edge of the worksurface.

Intermediate supports replace the need for other types of worksurface support when used with One-High or 1.5-High Universal storage. Steel top storage requires additional bracing inside the storage when used with an intermediate support (bracing is an option specified to match the width of the storage). Bracing is field-installed. Storage with laminate or wood tops do not require additional bracing.

Number of braces is determined by the orientation of the intermediate support to storage, not the orientation of the worksurface to storage: side-to-side (parallel) orientation requires one brace; front-to-back (perpendicular) orientation requires two braces.
Side-to-side (parallel) application allows worksurface to be oriented perpendicular to storage; front-to-back (perpendicular) application allows worksurface to be oriented in-line with storage.
Intermediate support must be at least 1" from the front, back, or side edges of the storage unit to allow clearance for installation.

On cabinets with steel tops (parallel or perpendicular applications), the intermediate support can be positioned left or right 1" or 7" from the side edge of the storage unit to align with bracing hole locations and can be positioned anywhere front to back. On cabinets with laminate or wood tops it can be positioned left or right anywhere between 1" and 7" from the side edge of the storage unit.

Worksurfaces 18"D or 24"D allow the intermediate support to be positioned below the worksurface 1" from the front or back. Worksurfaces 30"D require intermediate support centered below the worksurface.
Worksurface may extend up to 10" maximum overhang of intermediate support as long as the other end of the worksurface is anchored to the panel.
Surface materials: legs and intermediate support paint; spacer caps for panel attached legs black plastic only; glide cap for legs 6694 Slate only.

Closed, open, and half-loop legs are packed in boxes of six when ordered on the same line item. Bracing for intermediate supports ships separately from intermediate supports and is field installed into storage cases.

Infills are available in laminate and veneer and are used with open and closed loop FrameOne legs (both panel connected and freestanding versions) for added privacy. Connectors attach to the back side of the legs. Infills are available 24"W and 30"W.

Double post C-leg can be used on a single worksurface or in a shared application. Post leg can be used on a single worksurface; non-locking caster and glide versions are available. Column is 4" in diameter and can be used as a column support on a single worksurface; adjustable and non-adjustable versions are available.

Double post leg can be used as a column support on a single worksurface or to support a shared application. Support plate can be used with a double post leg to join and support two worksurfaces; plate is 14"D or 20"D and 3 11/16"W.
Adjustable-height leg adjusts from 25 1/2"H to 31 1/2"H in 3/4" increments; can be used with a single worksurface; locking caster and glide versions are available.
Legs support Systems Worksurfaces at 26"H nesting, 28 1/2"H standard, 40 7/8"H standing or 25 1/2"H to 31 1/2"H adjustable heights.
Legs for Systems Worksurfaces do not include alignment tabs; pilot holes help the installer locate the proper leg position under the worksurface. Post legs are always installed at a 45° orientation.
26"H nesting height legs allow worksurfaces to nest underneath an adjacent worksurface supported with 28 1/2"H legs or a panel-supported worksurface.

Post leg in conjunction with two cantilevers or center support panels can be used as column support for linking worksurfaces. Post leg in conjunction with a side support bracket can support the end of a visitor or taper-flat worksurface.
Two post legs can be used in place of one double post leg as column support for spanner, jetty, bubble jetty, bullet peninsula, and angled peninsula worksurfaces for added stability.
Standing-height post or double post legs can be used as column support in panel-mounted applications only.

Double post leg can be used in a shared application with a support plate, or as a column support for spanner, jetty, bubble jetty, bullet peninsula, angled peninsula, and linking peninsula worksurfaces in panel-mounted applications.

Column can be used on spanner, bullet peninsula, angled peninsula, linking peninsula, jetty, and bubble jetty worksurfaces in panel supported applications. For Answer Freestanding desk applications, column can be used on bullet peninsula and jetty worksurfaces. Column cannot be used in a shared application.
Column is not recommended for applications that include post legs (round vs elliptical shape). Use single or double post legs as a column support in applications that include other post legs.
Adjustable-height legs can be used to support the primary worksurface, or legs can support a worksurface in a nesting application.

P-edge profile worksurfaces include alignment slots to accept cabby legs as an alternative column support for visual consistency in applications that include tables with cabby legs. Panel-mounted spanner, bullet peninsula, linking peninsula, jetty, and bubble jetty worksurfaces accept two legs. Visitor and linking worksurfaces accept one leg.

Long worksurface spans must be supported with cantilevers, pedestals, legs, or other supports at least every 54". Reinforcing channel (TS7WKSPT) allows 60" for heavily loaded, up to 72" for lighter loads; must be specified separately.

Post legs, C-leg, and adjustable column: paint. Post leg caster: black plastic only. Adjustable-height leg colors: 4750 Champagne Metallic, 4798 Sterling Metallic, 4799 Platinum Metallic, 7207 Black, 7225 Sand, 7239 Midnight. Support plate and reinforcing channel: black paint only.
Freestanding Guidelines for Systems Worksurfaces: see page 182.

When planning an L-configuration with knife edge worksurfaces, two UFB flat brackets should be used to support the worksurfaces; a cantilever is not wide enough to support the gap where the knife edge worksurfaces come together.
Freestanding L-configuration should be avoided due to profile on the backside of the knife edge worksurface.
Compatible storage includes 25 1/2"H pedestal with freestanding conversion kit, box/file mobile pedestals, and 1-high storage.
Knife edge worksurface over 27"H storage (lateral or pedestal) can make files difficult to access; use a 25 1/2"H pedestal that is flush with the front edge of the worksurface.
Knife edge worksurfaces require reinforcement channels for unsupported spans greater than 48": TS7WKSPT39 for 54"W, TS7WKSPT for 60"W and 66"W, TS7WKSPT72 for 72"W worksurfaces.
Although a 25 1/2"H pedestal looks good with knife edge, it does not align with other storage (drawers and base trim do not align); use a box/file mobile pedestal instead.

End panels, 27"H standard pedestals, side support brackets and FrameOne legs for Universal do not align properly with knife edge worksurfaces; use cantilevers instead. Side support brackets will work to support the back end of a worksurface; the front end is where they won't align properly.
Edge-profile suffix appended to worksurface style number: none = laminate plastic 3 mm edge; P = laminate plastic P-edge; SW = wood with square edge (e.g., UJC3268L -> UJC3268LSW).
Full-depth jetty (WJ...) available only in laminate with plastic 3 mm edge (no P-edge, no wood).
Scallops are available only on visitor worksurfaces 36"W and wider; omit scallop option at no cost.
Wood (SW) and full-fill finish available only on UVC2424L/R and UVC3030L/R visitor worksurfaces (all others N.A.). Full-depth visitor/linking (WVC/WLC) laminate plastic 3 mm edge only.
Transaction worksurface style suffix identifies panel trim: TA thin trim, SA square trim, A oval trim. Wood not available for 30" panel width (UTR1630TA/SA/A).
Remember to specify cutout for power and data tray on the worksurface style number; door/tray (UTTR...) is ordered separately.
Power schematic, line and ground must be specified: 3+1 (line 1-4), 2+2 (line 1-4), or 3SN (line 1-3), each with system or isolated ground (no cost).
Remember to specify cutout for personal caddy on the worksurface style number. Specify brace: for 54"W and 60"W worksurface, or for 66"W and 72"W worksurface (no cost).
Answer panel junctions can accommodate only one cantilever at a seam.

Side support bracket (USSBR) is a pair of handed brackets; only one is required for rear corner support of panel-mounted corner worksurfaces. Specify one USSBR for every two corner worksurfaces in on-module applications. Order an additional supply for off-module fin wall applications.
Intermediate support bracing option: laminate or wood storage tops — no brace; steel storage tops — one brace or two braces (30", 36", or 42"W) +$47.
Corner worksurfaces require a leg in the back corner; order fifth leg if specifying a package of four.
See Table and Leg Combinations page (page 244) for number of adjustable-height legs required per worksurface.
Power/communication spheres are field installed; use a 3"-diameter drill to cut mounting hole. Power and communication port uses a 3 1/2"-diameter drill hole.
Grommet AWAG2 is for use on worksurfaces only.
15 3/4"L cable riser (DAVCE) is an extension only; it does not include attachment hardware or floor plate.
TS5SKLBNE, TS5SKEXT and TS5LEGCLP are Turnstone products (not Steelcase), with different pricing terms.

dimensions.subject: Universal Systems Worksurface
dimensions.text: Worksurface has a wood core with a High-Pressure Laminate or wood veneer surface and is 1 3/16" thick.

dimensions.subject: P-edge
dimensions.text: P-edge profile worksurface depths are 3/8" deeper than 3 mm edge profile worksurfaces.

dimensions.subject: Cord drop / scallops
dimensions.text: Worksurface depth is 1/2" less than nominal. Corner worksurface scallops 12 1/2" from rear corner to scallop center; taper-flat single scallop 18 1/2" from larger end.

dimensions.subject: Soft edge / door & tray / caddy
dimensions.text: Soft edge: width 36", depth 3", thickness 1/2" at front. Cutout for door: width 24", depth 4 5/8". Tray (below worksurface): width 27 1/8", depth 6", height 4 3/4". Caddy: width 10", depth 18", height 8".

dimensions.subject: Caddy cutout
dimensions.text: Cutout is 6 5/8" from edge of worksurface; bracing is 5 1/2" from the edge. Tray height 4 3/4"; outer tray width 27 1/8" (tray drawing: 6" x 4 3/4" x 27 1/8").

dimensions.subject: Panel-mounted supports actual dimensions
dimensions.text: Cantilever: height 12 1/4", depth 15 1/2", glide range N.A. Center support panel: height 28 1/2" or 40 7/8"*, depth 11", glide range 1 1/4". End panel: height 28 1/2" or 40 7/8"*, depth 23 3/4" or 29 3/4", glide range 1 1/4". *Height includes thickness of a worksurface.

dimensions.subject: FrameOne legs and supports
dimensions.text: Closed, open, and half-loop legs: height* 28 1/2", depth 24" or 30", glide range 2 1/4". Post leg: height* 28 1/2", glide range 1". Intermediate support for One-High storage: height* 28 1/2", height 11 1/4", depth 16", width 2 3/16". For 1.5-High storage: height* 28 1/2", height 5 1/4", depth 16", width 2 3/16". *Height includes thickness of the worksurface.

dimensions.subject: FrameOne / pedestals
dimensions.text: 27"H pedestal inside closed/open/half-loop leg: 3" gap (27 1/4" / 27 1/8" shown). Inside post leg: 5 3/4" gap. Intermediate support position on steel-top cabinets: 1" or 7" from side edge; minimum 1" from front/back/side edges.

dimensions.subject: FrameOne intermediate support overhang
dimensions.text: Worksurface may overhang intermediate support up to 10" max (other end anchored to panel).

dimensions.subject: Legs and columns actual dimensions
dimensions.text: Column: height* 28 1/2", glide range 1 1/2". Adjustable column: 28 1/2"–31 5/8", glide 3 1/8". Double post leg: 28 1/2" or 40 7/8", glide 3/4". Post leg: 26", 28 1/2", or 40 7/8", glide 3/4". Adjustable-height leg: 25 1/2"–31 1/2", glide 3/4". Double post C-leg: 28 1/2", glide 3/4". Support plate: N.A. (14"D or 20"D and 3 11/16"W). *Height includes thickness of a worksurface.
